steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Consumer Rights Act 2015 is the main law protecting consumers in contracts with businesses

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and as described — if not, the consumer has rights to reject, repair or replacement

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: For faulty goods, the consumer has 30 days to reject for a full refund; after 30 days, they can request repair or replacement

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: If a repair or replacement fails, the consumer is entitled to a refund (which may be reduced for use)

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the three statutory rights when buying goods? | Q: What remedies are available for faulty goods under the Consumer Rights Act 2015? | Q: What rights do consumers have when services are poor?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Goods must be of satisfactory quality, fit for purpose and match their description. After 30 days but within 6 months: repair or replacement. If repair or replacement fails: refund (may be reduced for use). After 6 months: con | Services must be performed with reasonable care and skill, within a reasonable time and at a reasonable price. If not, the consumer can require the trader to redo the service or, if that is impossible

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Know the three implied terms for goods (satisfactory quality, fit for purpose, as described) — always mention all three The 30-day short-term right to reject is a key reform of the 2015 Act — know the timeline of remedies Unfair terms are frequently tested — know examples and be able to explain why they are unfair Distinguish between remedies for goods, services and digital content — they differ slightly Know the roles of Trading Standards, CMA and Citizens Advice in enforcing consumer rights
